## How to use this template {.section-slide background-gradient="linear-gradient(160deg, #2b0836 0%, #1a0526 52%, #120118 100%)"}

This deck is a **reference sheet**, not a talk. Each slide demonstrates one
pattern from `juliacon2026.scss`. Copy the pattern you need into
`docs/slides/HeartRateLab.qmd` — see `README.md` in this folder for the merge
steps.

The section slides use a **JuliaCon 2026 violet gradient** (palette sampled from
the official Mainz banner), painted **edge-to-edge** by reveal's native background
layer — no white frame.

## Two-column layout

Standard Quarto/reveal `.columns` — no extra CSS needed, it inherits the theme.

## Callouts — reuse Quarto's native syntax

The four callout colors are remapped to the brand so you don't need any new
syntax — just the usual `::: {.callout-*}` fenced divs.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why context matters
`.callout-note` → Julia blue. Good for framing / method notes.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Typical range
`.callout-tip` → Julia green. Good for "within normal range" results.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Notably atypical
`.callout-important` → Julia red. Good for flagging elevated z-scores.
:::

## Stat highlights — echoes the poster's z-score forest

Use the `.jc-stat` span classes inline to call out a number the way the
poster's z-score table does:

- LF/HF ratio: [+2.64σ]{.jc-stat .jc-stat-elevated} — notably atypical
- SDNN: [+1.12σ]{.jc-stat .jc-stat-borderline} — slightly atypical
- RMSSD: [+0.03σ]{.jc-stat .jc-stat-typical} — typical


# Section dividers & down-slides {.section-slide background-gradient="linear-gradient(160deg, #2b0836 0%, #1a0526 52%, #120118 100%)"}

A `#` heading is **both** a full-bleed section divider **and the top of a
vertical stack**. Every `##` after it becomes a *down-slide* — press
<kbd>↓</kbd> (or <kbd>Space</kbd>) to descend. Try it now: there are three
down-slides below this one.

::: {.callout-note}
## How Quarto builds vertical stacks
`#` = new horizontal slide (stack top) · `##` after it = nested down-slides.
This nesting is automatic — no special class needed. Control the arrow-key
behaviour with `navigation-mode: linear` (right/space only, verticals flattened)
or leave the default (↓/↑ walk a stack, →/← jump between stacks).
:::

## Down-slide 1 of 3 ↓

This is the **first vertical child** of the section above.

- Reached by pressing <kbd>↓</kbd> from the divider, or <kbd>Space</kbd> to
  auto-advance through the whole stack.
- The slide number reads `c/t` (current / total) in the corner — vertical
  position is tracked too.

## Down-slide 2 of 3 ↓

Down-slides are ordinary content slides — they inherit the white theme, the
green heading pip, callouts, code blocks, everything.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Good use for a stack
Park optional detail / backup material as down-slides under a headline slide:
the audience sees the headline, and you drill down only if asked.
:::

## Down-slide 3 of 3 ↓

Last one in the stack. Pressing <kbd>→</kbd> (or <kbd>Space</kbd>) from here
jumps back up to the horizontal track and on to the closing slide.

```julia
# down-slides are authored as plain `##` headings under a `#` — nothing else
using HeartRateLab
m = read_txt("recording.txt")
```
